title: The Rockin' Chair story
summary: Roy tells of the first time at Meadowbrook he split the high note and later redeemed it against Harry James at the Palladium.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: I had one little incident there. We was playing 'Rockin' Chair'... Benny Carter had worked with them over at Meadowbrook, had made an arrangement on 'Rockin' Chair.' You know, Benny didn't know until he talked to me last year that he didn't make that arrangement for me? He thought that he had made that arrangement for me, and he made it for himself! But the way I did...my doing it and him doing it was two different things, you know.

So we were playing this thing, and it was... This is before I was sitting in the band I think this happened. Two ladies sitting down, old ladies sitting down in front of the band, they were eating this soup or something like that, and he called this 'Rockin' Chair.' And I couldn't say no. So the minute I walked out to play, they dropped this bowl, and said(?), 'Oh Christ. Because this Black dude, I know damn well he gonna blow us out of the joint.' I just had the feeling, because I could look at their disgust when I walked out, you know. Seeing me, the only Black face up there, you know.

So I got into the piece and everything. And so, when it got around there at the end, the band was high(?) and I had to play to get above the band. So I did that, and man, they were... I thought they were gonna have a fit. So I tried to hit the note on the end soft, and I split that fella in a million damn pieces! Well, I was embarrassed! And that always ....[MOTOR NOISE]...., that "Rockin' Chair." That's the reason when I made it, I was blind drunk.
Yeah. I don't know I could have got through it if I had been sober. I still had that thing on me from that hotel, you know.
Did you play that every night, "Rockin' Chair"?

No, that's the thing. I didn't play it every night. We probably played it at the wrong time, you know. Like, he pulled that on me once in the Palladium. We had a battle of music against Harry James. And that was a funny thing, man. All the things I had to play, he played nothing that I had to play all night long -- until the broadcast came. And way down in the broadcast, he's got "Rockin' Chair." And I had played very little Jazz all night long, which was rare for me, you know. In other words, it was like he would just set me aside for the night, you know. And I'm telling you, I went in training for that thing. For
two weeks I didn't drink, I didn't smoke, and I practiced every day, and I was ready for it, you know. But this here takes all the fun(?) out of it, you know.

But shit, things don't work out like that for people. They try, but it just don't work out. So what happened was that when he finally called this thing, man, I'd say the first two or three bars I was nervous as a dog, then all of a sudden, just something took a hold of me, and I just forgot about the crowd, the band and everything, and I played it. And I got to the end and I thought about them two old ladies, and I hit the F note, and it looked it was going to split -- and I screamed the loudest A you ever seen in your life. I just refused to let that thing go down there, you know. And I got a standing ovation.

So Gene tried to go into his next number. Couldn't make it. I had to play an encore. And he hated that, you know. So then he played "After You've Gone". It reminded me of Zutty. [SINGS OLD-TIMEY TEMPO] I mean, come on!
